text: Never introduce a bare class name that matches a reserved prefix line in css-scopes.txt (e.g. 'flex', 'card', 'page') without owning that module — the framework block is off limits entirely for anything new.
Always prefix a new class with its owning module's prefix (e.g. '.panel-grip', not '.grip') unless the selector already starts with the module's own class.

Before naming a class, grep-census the live CSS/JS for that name; a hit in another module is a collision and you must pick a different name — but check WHERE the hit is first, since vendored bundles (e.g. minified three.js) can false-positive.

A View subclass's constructor name is itself a CSS class (classify() kebab-cases the chain), so a class named Stage silently wears the framework's own '.stage' — check every view class name against the census too, not just literal class= strings.

A modifier class built by string concatenation (e.g. 'type-anchors-post ' + variant.key) is a class name too — put the module prefix inside the concatenated string itself, not just around it, and check every possible runtime value of the variable, not only the one literal visible in source.

Never start a new module's class with 'page-' unless the module is core/Page itself, since that is core/Page's reserved namespace — except a second core module that itself extends Page may register its own sub-namespace like 'page-layout-' or 'page-section-' in css-scopes.txt.

'page--<slug>' (two dashes) is the per-route instance stamp core/Page.class.js puts on every page, and it is a fixed, hard-coded convention — never repurpose the two-dash form for a different module's own naming.

When a module opens a new namespace, its first class must add one line to css-scopes.txt ('prefix-   owner'); if css-scopes.txt is outside your write fence, the reservation is still owed — write it into the module's own doc/decisions.md under Open instead of dropping it.

Before naming a '-card'/'-tile'/'-box' class, check it isn't just the framework's existing '.card' (a framed box) — the three spacing words are '.pad' for a page region, '.card' for a framed box, and an em unit for a control or row; ~180 hand-rolled duplicate card/tile classes existed sitewide before this was enforced.

It is only a guideline, not a hard rule, exactly which of '.pad' / '.card' / an em-based size a given box should use — the skill gives a rule of thumb (page region vs framed box vs control/row) but real layouts have judgment calls at the edges.
Skipping the whole new-css-class check is allowed, but only when reusing a class name that already exists — any genuinely new or renamed class name must go through the check.

One component gets one prefix used consistently for all its sub-parts (e.g. ui-<component>-*, panel-*, sidebar-*) rather than a fresh ad hoc name per sub-part — this is the general shape of every registered entry in css-scopes.txt, though the file does not state it as an explicit numbered rule.
